title: Kremlin and White House Confirm Putin, Xi and Trump Will Meet in Shenzhen on Nov. 19
dek: The Kremlin and the White House both say the three leaders will meet on the sidelines of APEC; Washington says nuclear arms reduction will be on the agenda, and a senior administration official said the U.S. does not expect a nuclear agreement.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The skyline of Shenzhen, China, the host city of the APEC summit

keyPoints: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Saturday that an agreement had been reached for a trilateral meeting on Nov. 19 in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of APEC, Anadolu reported.

The White House confirmed the meeting on Friday. Spokesperson Olivia Wales said Trump would conclude his China visit with the meeting, and that he planned to discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons, the South China Morning Post and Reuters reported.
A senior Trump administration official told Reuters, as reported by The Hindu, that the U.S. did not expect to reach any kind of agreement on nuclear arms.
China’s Foreign Ministry said on Nov. 6 that discussions were under way but that no agreement had been announced. Meridian has not found a Chinese government statement confirming the meeting itself.

Haaretz, reprinting an Associated Press report, says Trump plans to discuss the war against Iran with Putin and Xi at the meeting. The Jerusalem Post, citing the White House, reports Trump will raise the Iran war with Xi and Putin in China.
body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump are set to meet on Nov. 19 in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, according to statements from the Kremlin and the White House.

## What the Kremlin said

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state news agency TASS on Saturday: “An agreement has been reached to hold a trilateral meeting on the 19th between President Putin, Chairman Xi and President Trump.” [Anadolu reported](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/eurasia/kremlin-says-putin-xi-trump-to-hold-trilateral-meeting-in-shenzhen-on-nov-19/4125290) that Peskov said the meeting would take place in Shenzhen on the sidelines of APEC. Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov had said last month that the three capitals were ready in principle to hold the summit, and that Russia and the United States had not agreed on a separate bilateral meeting between Putin and Trump.

## What the White House said

The White House confirmed the plan on Friday. Spokesperson Olivia Wales said Trump “will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting,” [the South China Morning Post reported](https://scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3374415/white-house-confirms-us-china-russia-trilateral-apec-sidelines). Speaking on a call with reporters, Wales said Trump would discuss “the reduction of nuclear weapons” and that the meeting would take place on Thursday, Nov. 19, [The Hindu reported, citing Reuters](https://thehindu.com/news/international/donald-trump-to-raise-nuclear-arms-cuts-with-putin-xi-on-november-19-white-house-says/article71700773.ece). Reuters also reported that Trump leaves on Monday, Nov. 16, for a four-day Asia trip that includes a stop in the Philippines.

## Timing and context

Anadolu reported that the APEC summit is scheduled for Nov. 18 to 19 in Shenzhen, and that Trump said on Nov. 8 he expected to meet Putin and Xi there. China’s Foreign Ministry confirmed on Nov. 6 that discussions on the meeting were under way, before any agreement had been announced.

## Open questions

Reuters reported that Beijing has rebuffed attempts to discuss nuclear arms with Russia and the United States, and that China is hosting a summit focused on trade and commerce. Reuters also reported that Trump’s repeated insistence that the meeting focus on nuclear arms reductions has irritated China. A senior administration official told Reuters that the U.S. did not expect to reach any kind of agreement on nuclear arms.

Meridian has not found a Chinese government statement confirming the Nov. 19 meeting itself. The meeting has been described by the Kremlin and the White House. Meridian will update this story if Beijing confirms the meeting or if the agenda changes.

## Iran on the agenda

An Associated Press report, reprinted by Haaretz, says Trump plans to discuss the war against Iran with Putin and Xi at what it calls an unprecedented gathering in China, bringing together the leaders of the three largest nuclear powers. The Jerusalem Post reported that the White House said the Iran war and the possibility of reducing the three countries’ nuclear arsenals were among the issues on the agenda. A senior U.S. official cautioned that the first meeting is not expected to produce a nuclear arms agreement.
